sections.h2: What are my choices for selling a house in Johns Creek, GA?
sections.html:
A Johns Creek owner can list with an agent, sell without one, or take a cash offer, and the gap between those paths comes down mostly to time and condition. Johns Creek is a suburb in northeastern Fulton County, so closing steps and tax bills run through Fulton County as well as the city.

A traditional listing makes sense for a house that shows well. It exposes the property to the largest pool of buyers, though it also means staging, photos, inspections and a lender's appraisal. A sale by owner skips the commission but moves every task to you. A cash purchase trades price for speed and certainty.

  • Best for top price: a prepared listing with an agent who knows your school zone and subdivision.
  • Best for control: a sale by owner, if you are comfortable with contracts and disclosures.
  • Best for speed or condition problems: a cash buyer who takes the house as-is.

Whichever path you choose, collect the deed, the latest Fulton County tax bill, homeowner association documents if your subdivision has them, and any permits for work done on the house. Permit history matters in a city that runs its building permits through an online portal.

A high owner-occupancy rate means most Johns Creek sellers are living in the house or recently moved out of it, and most buyers will compare your house with other owner-occupied homes on similar lots. Households average 2.82 people, so the family-sized house is the typical comparison.

sections.h2: What should I know about Johns Creek before pricing my house?
sections.html:
Johns Creek is a young city. It incorporated on December 1, 2006, after a July 2006 referendum in northeast Fulton County, and the city says it is now the 10th largest in Georgia. It covers about 32 square miles roughly 25 miles north of Atlanta.

The city's own history page traces the area to trading posts on the Chattahoochee River in the early 19th century and to Technology Park/Johns Creek, a mixed-use business park that began in 1981 along McGinnis Ferry Road and Medlock Bridge Road. Today the city reports that about 25 percent of residents are international, with India, China and South Korea the largest groups. Recreation and Parks maintains more than 400 acres of parkland and nature reserve, with five access points to the Chattahoochee River.

  • Mail can carry a Johns Creek address with any of five ZIP codes: 30005, 30022, 30024, 30076 or 30097.
  • The city does not run garbage collection, so residents contract with private haulers.
  • Water comes through Fulton County, and power through Georgia Power or Sawnee Electric.
  • Police and fire service come from the city's own departments.

Buyers ask about those basics, so have the answers ready. Because the ZIP code on a mailing address can name a neighboring city, a buyer should confirm the property sits inside Johns Creek limits using the city's address tool.

sections.h2: Which schools serve Johns Creek homes?
sections.html:
Fulton County Schools serves Johns Creek. The city's schools page says 19 Fulton County public elementary, middle and high schools serve residents, and which one a child attends depends on the address and the attendance zone.

Eleven Fulton County elementary schools and one charter school serve the city, with names such as Abbotts Hill, Barnwell, Dolvin, Findley Oaks, Medlock Bridge, Ocee, Shakerag, State Bridge Crossing and Wilson Creek. Some of the elementary schools carry Roswell or Alpharetta mailing addresses even though they serve Johns Creek families. Four private schools also list themselves as serving the city: Holy Redeemer Catholic School, Mount Pisgah Christian School, Perimeter School and Woodward Academy North.

Zoning is address-specific, so do not tell a buyer which school a house feeds without checking. Direct buyers to Fulton County Schools to confirm the current zone for the exact address.

sections.h2: How do property taxes work for a Johns Creek house?
sections.html:
Johns Creek owners pay property tax to Fulton County, which includes the school system, and to the City of Johns Creek, and the bill arrives from the Fulton County Tax Commissioner. The city's new-resident FAQ states this directly.

Fulton County's Board of Assessors sets the value and mails a Notice of Assessment. The county says an owner can appeal the value within 45 days, and for 2026 most owners had until July 31, 2026, which has passed. Homeowners who qualified for a 2026 homestead exemption but missed the April 1 filing date could apply during that appeal period, and anyone who bought after January 1 applies for the 2027 tax year. Fulton County also says each notice now shows estimated tax savings, with discounts and exemptions, in place of an estimated tax figure.

  • Check the Fulton assessor's property search to confirm your exemptions are on the record.
  • Ask the Fulton County Tax Commissioner for the status of the current bill.
  • Ask your closing attorney how the year's tax will be split between you and the buyer.

sections.h2: What permits and code rules affect a Johns Creek sale?
sections.html:
Johns Creek runs building permits through an online customer self-service portal, and its permit process has six steps: application, fee payment, plan review, permit issued, required inspections and permit completed. The city also posts a Do I Need a Permit checklist.

If you finished a basement, built a deck or replaced a major system without a permit, a buyer's inspection may find it. The city's Code Compliance Division enforces the local ordinances and property maintenance code, and the nuisance and zoning ordinances are posted on its code regulations page. Ask Community Development whether any permit on your address is still open and close it out before you list.

The state's real estate transfer tax is a separate cost. Georgia's Department of Revenue prints the rate as $1 for the first $1,000 and 10 cents for each additional $100 or fractional part, and the seller is liable unless the contract says otherwise.

sections.h2: When should a Johns Creek owner consider a cash buyer?
sections.html:
A cash buyer is worth a look when you cannot or do not want to prepare the house for the retail market. In a city where buyers expect move-in condition at a high price, a dated or damaged house can sit, and carrying costs keep running while it does.

  • Inherited houses where the heirs live out of state.
  • Homes with deferred maintenance that would not pass a buyer's inspection.
  • Owners relocating on a short timeline.
  • Houses with unpermitted work that you would rather sell as it stands.

Ask for a written offer, read who pays the closing costs and transfer tax, and compare it with a net figure from a listing agent after commission and repairs.

faqs.q: Do I pay both city and county property tax in Johns Creek?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners pay Fulton County, which includes the school system, and the City of Johns Creek, and the combined bill comes from the Fulton County Tax Commissioner, according to the city's FAQ.

faqs.q: Is my Johns Creek mailing address always inside the city?
faqs.a: No. Johns Creek shares the ZIP codes 30005, 30022, 30024, 30076 and 30097 with neighboring cities. The city offers an address lookup tool to confirm whether a property is inside the limits.

faqs.q: Does Johns Creek pick up my trash?
faqs.a: No. The city says it does not provide garbage collection, and residents contract with private companies. A buyer will want to know which hauler serves the house.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal my 2026 Fulton County value?
faqs.a: No for most owners. The 2026 appeal deadline was July 31, 2026 unless another date was printed on your notice. Appeals run 45 days from each year's notice, and the value is what you can challenge, not the tax amount.

faqs.q: Who pays the Georgia transfer tax when I sell in Johns Creek?
faqs.a: The seller is liable under state law, though the sales contract often shifts it to the buyer. It must be paid before the deed is recorded, so confirm the assignment in the contract.
